source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: This Flexential facility is in one of the company national markets confirmed on its own homepage covering Oregon (Portland/Hillsboro), Texas (Dallas, Plano, Richardson), Ohio (West Chester, Cincinnati market), Kentucky (Louisville), Pennsylvania (Allentown, Collegeville, Philadelphia market), Virginia (Richmond), Minnesota (Chaska, Minneapolis market), and Arizona (Phoenix). Flexential was formed from the 2017 merger of ViaWest, founded 1999, and Peak 10, founded 2000, followed by a 2018 rebrand to Flexential. The company reports 40 plus data centers across 18 national markets, 3 million plus square feet of facilities, an 800 million dollar expansion investment, and a planned new campus on 110 acres in Kaufman County near Dallas. This specific state cluster was confirmed as an active Flexential market on the company own site, but no market specific founding, acquisition, or building history distinct from the general ViaWest and Peak 10 company story was located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
At 7.2 MW of published IT capacity, this campus is the largest by that measure among the three Pennsylvania facilities on this site that have published a figure, accounting for roughly 40 percent of the 18.2 MW total across those three. That share reflects the limits of what has been published, not a census of Pennsylvania's full data center inventory: 14 facilities are mapped in the state, and most publish no capacity number. The 7.2 MW figure is what the operator has stated; nothing beyond it has been published here.

Seven megawatts is a modest number by hyperscale standards, but its meaning for AI workloads depends on density. Assuming 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 7.2 MW of IT load supports roughly 180 racks, at 10 kW per rack, a figure more typical of colocation baseline deployments, it supports roughly 720 racks. The arithmetic is 7,200 kW divided by the assumed kilowatts per rack; neither result is the operator's claim. The 203,703 square feet of technical space is large relative to that power figure, implying an average floor density well below what dense GPU clusters require. A tenant filling that space at AI training densities would need more power than the published figure supports.

The certifications qualify this campus to host specific regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 address financial reporting controls and operational security controls respectively. PCI DSS qualifies it for cardholder data environments. ITAR qualifies it for controlled defense-related technical data. NIST 800-53 aligns it with federal security control frameworks. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. SSAE 18 is the auditing standard under which the SOC reports are issued, not a separate compliance regime. Which tenants occupy the facility is not published.
